You may have noticed we’re calling cartItems.get() here, instead of grabbing that useStore helper from our React / Preact / Solid / Vue examples. This is because useStore is meant to trigger component re-renders. In other words, useStore should be used whenever the store value is being rendered to the UI. Since we’re reading the value when an event is triggered ( addToCart in this case), and we aren’t trying to render that value, we don’t need useStore here. With our store in place, we can call this function inside our AddToCartForm whenever that form is submitted. We’ll also open the cart flyout so you can see a full cart summary.
